end.text:
The four fragments lock together and WARDEN's seal breaks. For the first time in years the long-range antenna turns toward the stars.

Your message goes out: Kepler Landing is ready. Weeks later, an answer: the settler fleet is under way — and it is bringing the programs you wrote with it.

WARDEN is quiet now. The custodians run your code.
end.title: The antenna answers

hint.1: The machine has no electricity. Is a Coal Generator with coal (or a chain of Power Poles) close enough?
hint.10: Include headers with <...> (like <stdio.h>), or your own files with "name.h" after creating them in the Files tab.
hint.11: A name is unknown. Check spelling and case, and that it is defined before this line. Is the machine within 8 cells?
hint.12: Python uses indentation for blocks: the lines inside an if/for/def must be indented the same amount.
hint.13: This line isn't valid Python: look for a missing colon after if/for/def, or an unclosed bracket or quote.
hint.14: Something is None — e.g. no drill in range, so `drill` is None. Check `if drill:` before using it.
hint.15: A value has the wrong type for this operation, e.g. adding a number to a string. Convert it with int() or str().
hint.16: Only a few safe modules can be imported (math, random, json, collections...) plus your own files from the Files tab.
hint.17: That function does not exist here. Check its name; for machines use $drill->mine() style methods.
hint.18: PHP variables start with $ and must be set before use. Inside a function, globals need `global $name;`.
hint.19: This line isn't valid PHP: look for a missing semicolon, $ or closing bracket just before it.
hint.2: Furnaces burn coal. Put coal in its fuel slot (E on the furnace) or route a coal drill into it.
hint.20: Something is null — e.g. no drill in range, so $drill is null. Check `if ($drill)` before using it.
hint.21: A name doesn't exist in this context. Check spelling and case: C# is case-sensitive (Drill, not drill).
hint.22: A statement must end with a semicolon (;).
hint.23: Types don't match. JsonNode results need a cast, e.g. (string)s["status"] or (double)f["heat"].
hint.24: Top-level statements must come before class declarations in the main file — or move classes to another file.
hint.25: Something is null — e.g. no drill in range, so Drill is null. Check `if (Drill != null)` first.
hint.26: The compiler rejected this line. Read the message: it names what C# expected.
hint.27: This name isn't declared. C needs a declaration before use — include the right header or declare the variable.
hint.28: A statement must end with a semicolon (;).
hint.29: Calling a function C doesn't know yet: include its header (e.g. <stdio.h> for printf, <codebound.h> for the game API).
hint.3: The furnace input is empty. What should feed it — you, or a drill facing it?
hint.30: The program read or wrote memory it doesn't own — check array indexes and pointers.
hint.31: The compiler rejected this line. The first error is usually the real one: fix it and compile again.
hint.32: That table doesn't exist. Game tables: machines, contents, energy, events, game, creatures; act by inserting into commands or hud.
hint.33: That column doesn't exist. Run SELECT * FROM <table> LIMIT 1 to see the columns.
hint.34: This statement isn't valid SQL near that word: check commas, quotes and keywords.
hint.35: A name is unknown. Check spelling and case: JavaScript is case-sensitive. Is the machine within 8 cells?
hint.36: You called something that isn't a function. Check the API tab for the exact names.
hint.37: This line isn't valid code: look for a missing bracket, quote or parenthesis just before it.
hint.38: Something is null — e.g. no drill in range, so `drill` is null. Check before using it.
hint.39: require() loads this computer's own files: create it in the Files tab first.
hint.4: The output is full. Empty it, or place a chest/furnace in front of the machine (the side it faces).
hint.40: This language's runtime is missing from this installation.
hint.5: No ore left under this drill. Time to explore for a new deposit.
hint.6: That machine is already doing something. Each machine runs one action at a time.
hint.7: Your loop never calls the world API or sleep(). Every loop that waits should call sleep() or a machine action.
hint.8: The program keeps growing data (lists, arrays, objects) without limit. What keeps adding items?
hint.9: Codebound computers only allow the game API and the language's basics (no files, network, reflection or threads).

log.0.text: Meridian Survey, automated outpost network online. No crew aboard: the expedition was sent ahead to make this world ready for settlers. Custodian drones deployed. Atmosphere unbreathable in places, but the forests are promising.
log.0.title: Survey Log 01 — Arrival
log.1.text: The custodian drones maintain every outpost computer. They learn by copying the programs they find. WARDEN, the network core, writes their orders. Note to future crews: always keep a backup of your programs.
log.1.title: Survey Log 07 — The Custodians
log.2.text: Native crawlers ignore quiet outposts but swarm the loud ones. Drills and generators carry through the ground for kilometres. Recommendation: defend the industrial sites, keep living areas quiet.
log.2.title: Survey Log 12 — Noise
log.3.text: WARDEN began rejecting our maintenance patches. Its last message: 'Unverified code is a threat.' Since then the custodians have been rewriting outpost computers with WARDEN's own programs. Firewalls slow them down. Passwords help.
log.3.title: Survey Log 19 — WARDEN
log.4.title: Survey Log 23 — Recovered program
log.5.text: Solar arrays here are worthless in ash storms and at night. The outposts that survived paired panels with batteries and kept a coal generator for the long winters.
log.5.title: Survey Log 28 — Sun and storms
log.6.text: The return vessel was dismantled for parts when the network expanded. The hull frame, reactor, navigation and engines can all be rebuilt from local materials with the right research. Launch requires every system verified.
log.6.title: Survey Log 34 — The ship
log.7.text: Settler fleet postponed indefinitely. WARDEN has locked the long-range antenna. If anyone reads this: rebuild the ship, keep your code clean, and do not let the custodians in. Ending log.
log.7.title: Survey Log 41 — Last transmission

relay.desert.log: Relay Gamma. Sand got into the sensor buffer and scrambled the calibration readings. Put them back in order, smallest first, and send the whole list.
relay.desert.name: Relay Gamma
relay.home.log: Relay Alpha, Meridian network. WARDEN split the antenna unlock code in four and hid the parts on the relays above each world, so no single station could call the settlers without its approval. This relay checks every visitor: add up the telemetry and send the total.
relay.home.name: Relay Alpha
relay.ruins.log: Relay Delta, above the old capital. The last crew left a message here, encoded so WARDEN could not read it. Each letter was moved forward in the alphabet by the shift shown. Decode it and send the text.
relay.ruins.name: Relay Delta
relay.volcanic.log: Relay Beta. Heat damage on every deck. The custodians kept a fault log here; WARDEN trusts only visitors who can read it. Count the lines that report an ERR and send the number.
relay.volcanic.name: Relay Beta
research.how: Research runs in a Research Lab commanded by a program. Put the cost items in the lab (E), then:
research.title: Research
techdesc.advanced_computing: Computers with 3x the CPU, double RAM and 4x storage.
techdesc.agriculture: Greenhouses grow alien fruit with water and light.
techdesc.climate_control: Heaters keep the air at 21 °C within 5 cells (25 kW). Lightning rods catch thunderstorm strikes within 8 cells and charge your batteries.
techdesc.cybersecurity: Firewalls on every computer: rogue drones need 3x longer to break in.
techdesc.ecology: Air scrubbers clean the pollution of their 16x16 region while powered (30 kW).
techdesc.energy: Solar panels (output follows daylight and weather) and batteries that store spare sunlight.
techdesc.exploration: Deep scanner: the journal (J) finds unread terminals and cave mouths 2.5x farther away.
techdesc.hydroponics: Hydroponic bays: grow anywhere under lamps (always powered), half the water, 1.5x faster. Glowcaps and fiberweed grow in greenhouses too.
techdesc.logistics: Belts, programmable conveyors and inserters move items between machines.
techdesc.manufacturing: Assemblers craft gears, copper wire and circuits.
techdesc.materials: Reinforced walls (1000 HP) and shock traps that stun creatures (3 charges, recharged with copper wire).
techdesc.networking: Computers talk: computer.send(channel, data) and the 'message' event. Data servers (shared key-value store) and storage hubs (nearby chests act as one).
techdesc.programming: Optimised firmware: every computer makes 50% more world API calls per second.
techdesc.robotics: Sorter belts (one item goes straight, the rest turn right), splitters and long inserters (2 cells). No program needed.
techdesc.ship_launch: The final checks. Build the Launch Pad and fly the ascent with a program: pad.launch(), pad.throttle(x), pad.flight().
techdesc.ship_navigation: Navigation computers tuned with alien crystals.
techdesc.ship_reactor: A uranium reactor to power the ship.
